title: The Footy Tipping (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist AFL Perth sport
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The footy tipping competition at the office has its annual launch
In February and the entry fee is five dollars on the haunch
Of the season ahead and everyone believes with full sincerity
That this year they've worked out the system with maturity

[Pre-Chorus]
I've been tipping in the same competition since ninety-six
And my method involves a coin and various statistics that don't fix

[Chorus]
The footy tipping knows something I don't know
It knows that random chance beats analysis for the show
The footy tipping has an office champion every year
Who wins by accident and won't admit the role played by sheer
Luck — that's my boy

[Verse 2]
There's always someone who gets round fifteen completely right
Through a system they describe as too complicated for light
Of day conversation — and then gets round sixteen completely wrong
And spends the rest of the season going back over the song

[Bridge]
In Perth it's AFL and the competition is close
And the footy tipping separates the reasonable from the most
Confident — which is not a correlation with correct
The footy tipping is democracy applied to what you select

[Outro]
Footy tipping knows… everyone thinks they know… footy tipping knows
That's my boy
